title: Synthetic bubble tests and readiness throttling to stabilize autoscaling
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Problem: In recent incidents our autoscaler over-reacts to transient readiness blips in cold-started regions, causing cascade scale-ups followed by rapid scale-downs and oscillation. This increases cost and temporarily degrades SLOs (p95 latency and request success) during region-onboarding and failover. Root cause analysis shows high fanout of health checks and lack of temporal smoothing for synthetic warmup checks.

Proposal: Implement a coordinated approach that combines small-traffic "synthetic bubble" probes (low-QPS, regional sticky origin) with an adaptive readiness throttle that attenuates readiness transitions for a short annealing window when a region or pool changes state. The system will: (1) run a buffered set of synthetic requests that exercise the full inference path at minimal cost, (2) use a weighted confidence score (recent synthetic success + real-traffic success) to mark instances as ready, (3) apply a throttling window (readiness attenuation) before publishing instance-level readiness to the autoscaler, and (4) integrate a soft eviction policy that prefers evicting instances with lower confidence when shedding load.

Why this is different: Unlike aggressive fanout reduction, synthetic bubbles provide actionable signals that validate model hot-path readiness without biasing production traffic. Readiness throttling reduces oscillation while preserving swift failover when confidence is high. The weighted eviction policy helps graceful degradation under memory/compute pressure.

Trade-offs: Adds modest synthetic QPS (budgeted), increases complexity in readiness scoring, and slightly lengthens failover time for marginal instances. However, the expected reduction in oscillation and cost outweighs the added latency during rare onboarding/failover events.

Success metrics: 50% reduction in autoscaler thrash events (scale up then down within 5 minutes), 30% fewer cost spikes during multi-region failover drills, and no regression to p95 latency SLO during normal traffic windows.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic bubble runner deployed in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with configurable QPS and origin sticky routing
Readiness confidence score computed per instance and stored in health index within 10s of test completion
Readiness attenuation window configurable (default 45s) and respected by autoscaler input feed
Eviction policy implemented: weighted eviction prefers low-confidence instances when memory pressure > 80%
Load tests show >=50% reduction in thrash events in the pre-prod failover sim harness
Runbook updated and on-call trained; no increase in customer-visible errors during rollout
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after incident analysis (INC-2026-02-18) showing rapid scale oscillation during eu-west-1 failover.
2026-02-24: Spike design review with Eng/PM/Observability. Decided on small synthetic QPS (<0.1% of region traffic) and sticky origin routing to avoid cross-region noise.
2026-03-01: Prototype synthetic bubble runner committed; initial smoke tests in sandbox passed (10/10 warmup requests succeeded).
2026-03-05: Implemented confidence scoring and attenuation window in health-agent; added metrics for synthetic_success_ratio and readiness_confidence.
2026-03-09: Integration test with autoscaler feed showed reduced scale triggers in controlled trials (pre-prod harness). Observability panel added.
2026-03-12: Started canary rollout to a subset of us-east-1 capacity pools; monitoring for unintended readiness delays.
Next steps: Expand canary to eu-west-1, run full multi-region failover drill, and tune attenuation window based on real traffic.
review_feedback: Marco Diaz (SRE): Keep synthetic QPS below 0.05% by default and provide throttles per-customer tier to avoid charging customers for probes.
Omar Haddad (Performance): Ensure synthetic requests run the same kernel path and KV-cache warm path as production; otherwise confidence is meaningless.
PM review (Nina Park): Add a flag to disable synthetic bubbles for Private deployments where customers may block synthetic traffic by policy.
test_plan: Unit tests for confidence scoring logic and attenuation timers
Integration tests in pre-prod with synthetic bubble enabled and disabled
Failure injection: drop synthetic responses to ensure autoscaler still falls back correctly
Chaos test: abrupt region join/leave while measuring thrash events and p95 latency
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable in 5% of us-east-1 pools for 72h; validate metrics
Phase 2 (regional expansion): Add eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 pools for 7 days
Phase 3 (full): Flip feature flag cluster-wide with 1-hour annealing windows and monitoring alarms
Rollback: Feature flag off; autoscaler reverts to existing readiness input
notes: Budget: synthetic bubbles estimated at ~0.02% of total token throughput for default config; finance ok'd the budget under Autoscale Stability Initiative
Ops: add alert when synthetic_success_ratio < 80% for >2m; route to on-call and trigger smoke job
Security: synthetic requests must preserve tenant isolation; use dedicated probe API keys scoped to read-only observability
